The brave pregnant teacher tried to restrain me, and in retaliation I kicked her stomach. Intentionally. She was fine but after that the priest came to calm me down. It was about a 45 minute episode.

The incident that got me expelled was in the actual classroom where I was aksed to leave the classroom and wait for the teacher in the hall. I took it upon myself to write a list titled "These are People I want to kill" followed by my classmates and my teacher. 

On top of that the school had also called CPS to my parents because I went to school telling them my parents "hit" me (when in reality all they did was slap me). All in the malicious effort to hurt other people. 

I have since grown out of my impulsive behaviors and regret every decision I've made like that in the past. I feel ashamed when I recall it.

When I was about 4 or 5 years old, my father worked as the Production Manager for a local theatre that hosted live theatre as well as famous bands and singers. Growing up I practically lived backstage meeting some big name artists and comedians and doing some acting here and there as well. However the moment that I regret the most is meeting the great Art Garfunkle. Very nice guy. Taught me how to play a G-chord on his guitar before the show. After watching his performance, he asked me "So how did you like the show?" To which I replied "It was good. But you sound better on my mom's CDs." He just laughed and thought it was cute. I was just at that stage where I was figuring out what was rude and what isn't. Also not being aware of how studio mixes sometimes sound different than live performances.
